intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through the iconic towers and intricate bas-reliefs of Angkor Wat, then continue to the mysterious Bayon temple with its 216 serene stone faces and the jungle-engulfed Ta Prohm temple made famous by Tomb Raider.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Historical Landmarks Tour
experiences.description: Visit the sobering Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) and the Killing Fields of Choeung Ek to understand Cambodia's tragic Khmer Rouge history, followed by the stunning Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda to appreciate the country's royal heritage and Buddhist culture.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine Koh Rong Samloem island and spend the day on Saracen Bay's crystal-clear turquoise waters and powdery white sand beaches. Snorkel among vibrant coral reefs, spot bioluminescent plankton at night, and enjoy the untouched natural beauty of Cambodia's finest beach destination.
experiences.location: Saracen Bay, Koh Rong Samloem, Sihanoukville

experiences.name: Siem Reap Street Food & Cooking Class
experiences.description: Begin with a guided tuk-tuk tour of Siem Reap's vibrant Pub Street night market sampling local street foods like Amok fish curry, Lok Lak beef, and fried insects if you dare. Then join a hands-on Khmer cooking class where a local chef teaches you to prepare traditional dishes using fresh ingredients from the Old Market.
experiences.location: Pub Street & Old Market (Psar Chas), Siem Reap

experiences.name: Tonle Sap Floating Village Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the extraordinary floating villages of Kampong Phluk on Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake, Tonle Sap. Witness entire communities built on stilts and floating platforms, visit a flooded mangrove forest by rowboat, and interact with local fishing families to gain deep insight into Cambodia's unique water-based way of life.
experiences.location: Kampong Phluk Floating Village, Tonle Sap Lake, Siem Reap

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phnom Penh or Siem Reap International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked tuk-tuk or airport shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at a 24-hour convenience store or airport food stall upon arrival — try instant noodles or a local snack for under $2 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange a small amount of USD or Khmer Riel at the airport for immediate expenses. Cambodia widely accepts USD. Keep arrival transport costs low by pre-booking a shared shuttle ($5–$10 USD) rather than a private taxi. Confirm hotel check-in is available for late arrivals.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get oriented. Explore the immediate coastal area, watch local fishermen, and soak in the scenery of the Gulf of Thailand coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby local market (fresh market) in the closest town — likely Kep or Sihanoukville depending on resort location. Browse fresh produce, street food, and local handicrafts. Visit the Crab Market in Kep if accessible, a famous local landmark where fishermen sell fresh seafood daily.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed sunset stroll on the beach. Head to a local beachside restaurant for a casual dinner. Watch the sun dip below the horizon over the Gulf of Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast at the resort or a nearby local café — try 'bai sach chrouk' (pork and rice) for $1.50–$2 USD.
meals.lunch: Street food at the local market — fresh spring rolls, grilled corn, or a bowl of 'kuy teav' (noodle soup) for $1–$2 USD.
meals.dinner: Beachside seafood shack near the resort — grilled fish or crab with rice for $4–$6 USD. Kep's Crab Market area has excellent budget options.

day_by_day.notes: November is the start of the dry season in Cambodia — expect warm, sunny weather with low humidity. Perfect beach weather. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen. Budget tip: eat where locals eat for the best prices.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kep National Park (if near Kep area). Hike the jungle trail loop (approximately 8 km) through the forested hillside with ocean views. The trail passes old French colonial villa ruins, offering a fascinating blend of history and nature. Entrance fee is minimal ($1–$2 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ruins of Kep's abandoned French colonial villas — a hauntingly beautiful reminder of Cambodia's turbulent history under the Khmer Rouge. These eerie, overgrown mansions are free to explore and provide incredible photo opportunities and historical context.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beachfront area. Visit a local night market if available, or relax at a hammock bar on the beach. Try a fresh coconut ($1 USD) as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or guesthouse breakfast — French baguette with condensed milk coffee (a Cambodian staple influenced by French colonialism) for $1–$2 USD.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the market before the hike — fresh fruit, bread, and snacks for under $3 USD.
meals.dinner: Local Khmer restaurant near the resort — try 'amok trey' (fish amok, a traditional Cambodian curry steamed in banana leaves) for $3–$5 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring plenty of water for the national park hike. The colonial ruins are a powerful reminder of Cambodia's complex history — be respectful. Mosquito repellent is recommended in forested areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget boat trip to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — one of Cambodia's most beautiful and undeveloped islands, just a 20-minute boat ride from Kep pier. Cost is approximately $5–$7 USD return. Arrive early to enjoy pristine beaches before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon snorkeling, swimming, and relaxing on Rabbit Island's white sand beaches. Rent a snorkel set from local vendors ($2–$3 USD) and explore the coral reefs. The island has no roads or vehicles — pure natural tranquility.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland by late afternoon boat. Freshen up at the resort and enjoy a quiet evening. Visit a local bar or beach café for a $1 Angkor beer and reflect on the day.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the resort before departing early — rice porridge ('bobor') or eggs for $1.50–$2 USD.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood BBQ on Rabbit Island — grilled fish, squid, or prawns cooked by local families on the beach for $4–$6 USD. Eat where the island residents eat.
meals.dinner: Back on the mainland, try a local Khmer family restaurant — 'lok lak' (stir-fried beef with pepper sauce and rice) for $3–$4 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm boat departure times at Kep pier the evening before. Last boats typically return by 5:00 PM. Bring cash as there are no ATMs on Rabbit Island. Pack sunscreen, a hat, and a reusable water bottle. November weather should be ideal for island visits.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a budget bus or shared taxi from Kep/Sihanoukville area toward Phnom Penh (approximately 3–4 hours, $5–$8 USD with operators like Giant Ibis or Mekong Express). Enjoy the countryside scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh and check into a budget guesthouse or hostel ($8–$15 USD/night). Head to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda complex (entrance $10 USD) — a stunning display of Khmer architecture, sacred Buddha statues, and the famous floor made of 5,000 silver tiles.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Sisowath Quay (the riverside promenade) as the city comes alive at dusk. Watch the confluence of the Mekong and Tonle Sap rivers. Browse street food stalls and soak in the vibrant city atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab food at a roadside stall before the bus — 'num pang' (Cambodian baguette sandwich with pâté and vegetables) for $0.75–$1 USD.
meals.lunch: Bus stop meal or packed snacks — fruit and crackers for $1–$2 USD.
meals.dinner: Riverside street food along Sisowath Quay — grilled skewers, fried rice, or noodles from vendors for $2–$3 USD. Try the famous 'nom banh chok' (Khmer noodles with fish gravy).

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets in advance online for better prices and guaranteed seats. Giant Ibis is highly recommended for safety and comfort on a budget. Store valuables securely in Phnom Penh — it is a bustling capital city. Budget accommodation options include Mad Monkey Hostel or Eighty8 Backpackers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply moving and historically essential site. This former high school was converted into a torture prison by the Khmer Rouge. Entrance fee is $8 USD. Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough visit. This is one of the most important historical sites in Southeast Asia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk ($3–$5 USD) to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial, located 15 km outside the city center. Rent an audio guide ($3 USD) for a comprehensive and deeply respectful experience. This UNESCO-recognized memorial is sobering but essential for understanding Cambodia's modern history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center. Visit Phnom Penh Night Market (Phsar Reatrey) for shopping and street food. Browse local handicrafts, scarves, and souvenirs at negotiable prices.

meals.breakfast: Local breakfast spot near your guesthouse — 'bai sach chrouk' (pork and rice) or French bread with eggs for $1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Simple Khmer restaurant near Tuol Sleng — rice with mixed vegetables and tofu or chicken for $2–$3 USD.
meals.dinner: Night market food stalls — try 'cha kdav' (stir-fried vegetables), grilled meats, and fresh fruit smoothies for $3–$4 USD total.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — take breaks if needed and be respectful of the space. Photography is permitted but must be done tastefully. These sites are critical for understanding Cambodia's history and the resilience of its people. Dress modestly out of respect.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the National Museum of Cambodia (entrance $10 USD) — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer art, including pre-Angkorian and Angkorian sculptures, bronzes, and ceramics dating back to the 4th century. Beautifully set in a traditional red-painted Khmer building.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco building from the 1930s. Browse everything from jewelry and electronics to fresh food and clothing. Practice your bargaining skills for souvenirs. Then visit Wat Phnom, the hilltop temple that gave Phnom Penh its name (entrance $1 USD).
day_by_day.evening: Take a sunset cruise on the Mekong River — budget operators offer $5–$8 USD per person for a 1-hour boat ride with beautiful views of the city skyline and river life.

meals.breakfast: Café near the museum — iced coffee with condensed milk and a pastry for $2 USD.
meals.lunch: Central Market food court — fresh noodles, fried rice, or Khmer curry for $1.50–$2.50 USD.
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant on Sisowath Quay — 'fish amok' or 'beef lok lak' with a cold Angkor beer for $5–$7 USD total.

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum is closed on public holidays — check in advance. The Central Market is best visited in the morning when it is less crowded. Sunset cruises can be booked directly at the riverside for the best prices — avoid hotel-arranged tours which add a markup.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an overnight or morning bus from Phnom Penh to Siem Reap (approximately 5–6 hours, $6–$12 USD). Alternatively, take a speedboat along the Tonle Sap Lake ($35 USD — a splurge but a unique experience). Arrive in Siem Reap and check into a budget guesthouse on Pub Street area ($8–$15 USD/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Siem Reap town center. Walk through the Old Market (Phsar Chas) for local goods and snacks. Visit the Angkor National Museum ($12 USD) to prepare yourself with historical context before visiting the temples — an excellent investment before the Angkor complex.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Pub Street and the surrounding alleyways. Enjoy the lively atmosphere with street performers, food stalls, and budget bars. Try a $0.50 USD draft beer at one of the famous cheap beer bars.

meals.breakfast: Bus station or guesthouse breakfast — rice or bread with eggs for $1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Old Market food stalls in Siem Reap — fresh spring rolls, grilled pork skewers for $2 USD.
meals.dinner: Pub Street area — 'Khmer BBQ' (table grill with meats and vegetables) at a budget restaurant for $5–$7 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets to Siem Reap in advance, especially during peak season (November–February). Giant Ibis and Mekong Express are reliable budget options. Siem Reap guestthouse recommendations: Onederz Hostel, Lub d, or Mad Monkey. The Angkor Archaeological Park 3-day pass ($62 USD) is the best value — purchase it at the official ticket office, not from touts.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 4:30 AM for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise — one of the most breathtaking sights in the world. Arrive at Angkor Wat ($62 USD for 3-day pass) before dawn and position yourself at the reflecting pool for the perfect reflection shot. Spend the morning exploring the massive 12th-century temple complex — the world's largest religious monument.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom (the Great City) — explore the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Terrace of the Elephants, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the day ($12–$15 USD) to navigate between sites efficiently.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ta Prohm temple — famously known as the 'Tomb Raider temple' — where massive silk-cotton trees grow through the ancient stone ruins. The late afternoon light filtering through the jungle canopy is magical. Return to Siem Reap for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks and water the night before for the pre-dawn departure — bananas, crackers, and a thermos of coffee.
meals.lunch: Temple complex food stalls near Angkor Thom — rice dishes and fresh coconuts for $2–$3 USD. Bring extra water.
meals.dinner: Local Khmer restaurant near the Old Market — 'samlor korko' (traditional vegetable and pork soup) and rice for $3–$4 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly at all temple sites — shoulders and knees must be covered. Bring a hat, sunscreen, and at least 2 liters of water per person. November weather is ideal — dry and not too hot. Negotiate your tuk-tuk price the evening before for a full-day rate. A reputable tuk-tuk driver can be arranged through your guesthouse.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Angkor Archaeological Park for Day 2 of your 3-day pass. Explore the Banteay Srei temple (approximately 25 km north of Siem Reap) — known as the 'Citadel of Women' and famous for its intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest examples of Khmer art. Also visit Banteay Samré temple nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the floating villages on Tonle Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Take a budget boat tour ($8–$10 USD) to see the unique stilt-house communities and floating schools. This is a fascinating cultural and geographical experience unlike anywhere else in the world.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Cambodia — return to Siem Reap for a farewell dinner. Visit the Angkor Night Market for last-minute souvenir shopping. Enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance at a local restaurant (some offer free shows with dinner purchase).

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café — 'bai sach chrouk' and iced coffee for $2 USD.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or temple area food stall near Banteay Srei — noodles or rice with vegetables for $2 USD.
meals.dinner: Farewell Khmer feast at a mid-range local restaurant — order a spread of traditional dishes including fish amok, lok lak, and mango salad for $6–$8 USD per person. Toast with an Angkor beer ($1 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Use your remaining days on the 3-day Angkor pass wisely — it is valid for any 3 days within a 10-day window. Banteay Srei requires a tuk-tuk or motorbike — negotiate a half-day rate of $10–$12 USD. The Tonle Sap Lake boat tours can be arranged through your guesthouse or at the lake dock. Be aware of tourist pricing at the lake — compare a few operators before booking. Begin packing and confirm any onward travel arrangements for the following day.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Phnom Penh International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack or room service at the resort after arrival

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — arrival is late at night. Confirm your transfer from the airport in advance. Exchange some USD or withdraw Cambodian Riel (KHR) at the airport for small expenses.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery after travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a morning stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings and soak in the coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach town area near the resort. Visit nearby markets or a local village to get a feel for Cambodian coastal life. Pick up a SIM card and grab a refreshing coconut from a beachside vendor.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the beach followed by dinner at a beachside seafood restaurant. Enjoy fresh grilled fish and Khmer-style curry while watching the sun dip into the Gulf of Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Casual beachside cafe — try Lok Lak (stir-fried beef) or Amok fish with rice (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Local seafood restaurant near the resort — grilled prawns, squid, and steamed rice (~$10–15)

day_by_day.notes: November is the start of the dry season in Cambodia — expect sunny skies and comfortable temperatures around 28–32°C. Perfect beach weather.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided snorkeling or island-hopping boat trip to nearby islands (if near Sihanoukville or Kep area). Explore coral reefs and crystal-clear waters of the Gulf of Thailand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the island trip and relax on the resort beach. Rent a kayak or paddleboard from the resort for some light water activity. Alternatively, visit a local fishing village to observe traditional Cambodian coastal culture.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Apsara dance performance or cultural show if available locally. Dine at a mid-range Khmer restaurant in town.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort — eggs, tropical fruit, and Cambodian rice porridge (Bobor)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the boat or island snack bar — fresh fruit and sandwiches
meals.dinner: Khmer restaurant in town — try Fish Amok (national dish), Samlor Korko soup, and sticky rice (~$10–12)

day_by_day.notes: Book island-hopping tours through the resort or a local travel desk. Tours typically cost $15–25 per person and include snorkeling gear. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kep National Park (if near the Kep/Kampot region). Hike through jungle trails with views over the Gulf of Thailand. Look out for wildlife including butterflies, monkeys, and tropical birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the famous Kep Crab Market — a beloved Cambodian institution. Watch fishermen bring in their catch and browse fresh seafood stalls. Learn about the local crab pepper trade that Kep is famous for.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a hilltop bar or rooftop venue with panoramic coastal views. Return to the resort for a relaxing evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Kep Crab Market — fresh Kampot pepper crab, grilled corn, and seafood skewers (~$8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby mid-range eatery — Khmer red curry with jasmine rice (~$10–14)

day_by_day.notes: Kep is approximately 1–2 hours from Sihanoukville by road. Hire a tuk-tuk or private driver for the day (~$25–35). Kampot pepper is world-renowned — buy some as a souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart early for Phnom Penh by bus or private transfer (4–5 hours from the coast). Check into a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel in the city center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda in Phnom Penh. Admire the stunning Khmer architecture, the Emerald Buddha, and the meticulously maintained palace grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Phnom Penh Riverside Promenade (Sisowath Quay). Enjoy the lively atmosphere, street food vendors, and views of the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers meeting point.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route — Banh Mi sandwich or rice with grilled pork (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Phnom Penh — try Khmer BBQ or a set dinner menu (~$12–18)

day_by_day.notes: Book your bus or private transfer in advance. Giant Ibis or Mekong Express buses are comfortable and reliable (~$12–15). The Royal Palace closes at noon for lunch; plan to arrive before 11:30 AM or after 2:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply moving and historically important site documenting the Khmer Rouge era. Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough visit with an audio guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial, located about 15 km from the city center. This UNESCO-recognized site offers a profound and essential understanding of Cambodia's 20th-century history.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) for souvenir shopping — silk scarves, silver jewelry, and local crafts. Wind down with dinner at a well-regarded local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or nearby cafe — French baguette with eggs and coffee (Phnom Penh has a strong French colonial cafe culture)
meals.lunch: Local Khmer restaurant near Tuol Sleng — rice with fish curry and fresh spring rolls (~$6–8)
meals.dinner: Romdeng Restaurant (social enterprise serving traditional Khmer cuisine) or similar — 3-course Khmer dinner (~$15–20)

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Killing Fields visits are emotionally heavy. Take your time, be respectful, and allow space for reflection. Both sites charge a small entrance fee (~$3–5 each). Hire a tuk-tuk for the day (~$15–20).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early morning flight or bus to Siem Reap (1-hour flight or 6-hour bus). Check into your mid-range hotel near the Old Market area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for an excellent introduction to Angkor civilization before visiting the temples. This sets the historical context perfectly for the next two days.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pub Street and the Old Market area. Browse local handicraft stalls, silk shops, and art galleries. Enjoy a traditional Khmer dinner with cultural performance.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before travel — Cambodian rice porridge or baguette
meals.lunch: Restaurant near Angkor National Museum — Khmer noodle soup or rice dishes (~$6–9)
meals.dinner: Cuisine Wat Damnak or Mahob Restaurant — contemporary Khmer cuisine in a mid-range setting (~$15–20)

day_by_day.notes: Book flights from Phnom Penh to Siem Reap in advance (~$40–70 one way). Alternatively, Giant Ibis bus is comfortable and affordable (~$13). Purchase your Angkor temple pass upon arrival or online — a 3-day pass is ~$62.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn start to watch sunrise at Angkor Wat — one of the most iconic experiences in Southeast Asia. Arrive by 5:00 AM to secure a good spot by the reflecting pools. Explore the outer galleries and bas-reliefs as the light improves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Angkor Wat complex in depth, then visit Angkor Thom — the great walled city. See the Bayon Temple with its 216 enigmatic stone faces, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ta Prohm Temple (the 'Tomb Raider' temple) as the afternoon crowds thin out. Marvel at the massive tree roots engulfing ancient stone structures. Return to Siem Reap for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed snack or energy bar before sunrise; proper breakfast after at a cafe near the temples (~$4–6)
meals.lunch: Temple-area restaurant or packed lunch — Khmer fried rice, spring rolls, fresh fruit (~$6–8)
meals.dinner: Siem Reap restaurant — try Amok, Lok Lak, and mango sticky rice for dessert (~$12–16)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the day (~$15–20) — they know the best routes and timing. Wear comfortable walking shoes, light breathable clothing, and bring plenty of water. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) as temples are sacred sites.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the outer Angkor temples: Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women' known for its intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered among the finest in Khmer art. Then visit Banteay Samre, a lesser-visited but beautifully preserved temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the floating villages on Tonle Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Take a boat tour through the stilted villages, observe the unique way of life of the lake-dwelling communities, and learn about their fishing traditions.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Apsara dance performance at a dedicated cultural venue in Siem Reap. This classical Khmer dance form is a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. Enjoy a farewell dinner in Siem Reap.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local bakery — croissant, tropical fruit plate, and iced coffee
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Tonle Sap — fresh fish dishes and Khmer noodles (~$7–10)
meals.dinner: Dinner and Apsara show package at a cultural restaurant (~$20–30 including show)

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is about 25 km north of Siem Reap — negotiate a full-day tuk-tuk rate (~$20–25). The Tonle Sap boat tour costs approximately $10–15 per person. The Apsara show is a must-see cultural highlight — book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cambodia — visit the Siem Reap Artisans Angkor workshop to see skilled craftspeople creating traditional Khmer silk weaving, stone carving, and lacquerware. Shop for high-quality, ethically made souvenirs that support local artisans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute exploration of the Old Market (Phsar Chas) for souvenirs — Cambodian spices, silk scarves, handmade jewelry, and local coffee. Enjoy a final Cambodian lunch before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Siem Reap International Airport for departure. Reflect on an incredible 10-day journey through Cambodia's beaches, history, and culture.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy a full spread one last time
meals.lunch: Old Market area cafe — Khmer sandwich (Num Pang), fresh juice, and mango sorbet (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or light snack before departure

day_by_day.notes: Artisans Angkor is free to enter and highly recommended for ethical souvenir shopping. Allow 3 hours before your flight for airport check-in. Keep some USD for airport taxes or last-minute purchases. Cambodian Riel cannot be exchanged outside the country, so spend any remaining KHR before departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrival at Phnom Penh International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer vehicle will be waiting to escort you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon check-in, enjoy a welcome amenity — chilled towels, tropical fruit basket, and a complimentary glass of Champagne prepared by the resort's concierge team.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome platter arranged by the resort — fresh local fruits, artisan cheeses, and a selection of Cambodian finger foods served in-suite upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night. Keep Day 1 relaxed. Confirm your 10-day itinerary preferences with the concierge upon check-in. Request a 9:00 AM wake-up call and a full breakfast reservation for the following morning. Ensure luggage is unpacked and essentials are set out for an early start on Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up to a leisurely resort breakfast with ocean views. Afterward, take a private guided orientation walk along the beachfront surrounding Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the local coastal village nearby, visiting a traditional Cambodian fishing community to learn about their way of life, boat-building traditions, and morning catch rituals. Your private guide will provide cultural context and historical background on the coastal regions of Cambodia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the resort's luxury amenities — spend time at the infinity pool overlooking the sea, book a 90-minute traditional Khmer massage at the resort spa using local herbs and oils, or take a private snorkeling excursion along the nearby reef arranged by the resort's water sports team.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar, followed by a private candlelit dinner on the beach. The resort's executive chef will prepare a curated five-course tasting menu featuring fresh Cambodian seafood — lobster, tiger prawns, and local reef fish — paired with premium wine selections.

meals.breakfast: Grand buffet breakfast at the resort's main restaurant — tropical fruits, freshly baked pastries, Cambodian congee (bobor), eggs to order, and fresh-pressed juices.
meals.lunch: Casual poolside lunch at the resort's beach club — grilled barracuda, mango salad, and coconut water served in the shell.
meals.dinner: Private five-course beachfront dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — Cambodian seafood tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day after the late arrival. Keep the pace relaxed. Confirm upcoming day-trip bookings with the concierge, particularly private transport and guide arrangements for Angkor Wat.

day_by_day.morning: Private chartered flight or luxury speedboat transfer (arranged by the resort) to Siem Reap — the gateway to the Angkor Archaeological Complex. Upon arrival, check into a pre-arranged luxury day suite at a premium Siem Reap property (such as Amansara or Belmond La Résidence d'Angkor) for freshening up. Begin a private guided tour of Angkor Wat at dawn's second light — explore the iconic five-towered temple, its bas-relief galleries depicting Hindu epics, and the sacred reflecting pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Angkor exploration with a private tour of the Bayon Temple at Angkor Thom — marvel at the 216 serene stone faces carved into its towers. Visit the Elephant Terrace and the Terrace of the Leper King. Enjoy a private picnic lunch prepared by your hotel in a scenic shaded area within the temple complex.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town for a cultural evening — attend a private Apsara dance performance at a heritage venue, followed by a premium dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak, one of Cambodia's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants specializing in modern Khmer cuisine using indigenous ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure or en route.
meals.lunch: Gourmet private picnic within the Angkor complex — prepared bento boxes with Cambodian-inspired flavors, fresh fruit, and chilled beverages.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Cuisine Wat Damnak, Siem Reap — modern Khmer tasting menu with local herbs, fermented fish, and seasonal produce.

day_by_day.notes: November weather in Siem Reap is ideal — dry season with mild temperatures. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sun protection. Respectful attire (covered shoulders and knees) is required inside temple complexes. Overnight in Siem Reap or return to resort based on preference — confirm with concierge in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private sunrise visit to Ta Prohm — the legendary 'jungle temple' famously featured in the film Tomb Raider, where ancient tree roots dramatically engulf the stone ruins. Enjoy the mystical atmosphere before the crowds arrive. Your private guide will narrate the temple's history as a Buddhist monastery built by King Jayavarman VII in the late 12th century.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' a 10th-century temple renowned for its extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings. Often considered the finest example of Khmer decorative art, this smaller temple is a photographer's paradise. Afterward, visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for an immersive deep-dive into Khmer civilization, artifacts, and the history of the Angkor Empire.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort via private luxury transfer. Enjoy a relaxing evening at the resort — perhaps a couples' spa treatment or a private yoga session on the beach at sunset, followed by dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Siem Reap hotel or resort before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium riverside restaurant in Siem Reap — try Malis Restaurant for elevated traditional Khmer cuisine in a beautiful garden setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — fresh seafood and Cambodian specialties with a curated cocktail menu.

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is approximately 25 km north of Siem Reap — factor in travel time. The Angkor National Museum closes at 6:00 PM. Confirm private transfer back to the resort is pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury day trip to Phnom Penh — Cambodia's vibrant capital city. Depart early by private vehicle or chartered flight. Begin with a historically significant and deeply moving visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison), guided by a knowledgeable private historian who will provide context on the Khmer Rouge era and its profound impact on Cambodian society.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Palace and the Silver Pagoda — a stunning complex of royal buildings featuring the iconic Khmer-style rooflines, the Throne Hall, and the Silver Pagoda housing the Emerald Buddha and a life-sized gold Buddha encrusted with diamonds. Stroll through the surrounding gardens. Afterward, explore the National Museum of Cambodia, home to the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the Mekong and Tonle Sap rivers. Enjoy dinner at Topaz Restaurant — one of Phnom Penh's most prestigious fine-dining establishments offering French-Cambodian fusion cuisine. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Khéma Restaurant, Phnom Penh — a French-inspired brasserie with premium Cambodian ingredients in a colonial-era setting.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Topaz Restaurant, Phnom Penh — French-Cambodian fusion with an extensive wine cellar and elegant atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng Museum is a deeply emotional experience — approach with sensitivity and allow sufficient time. The Royal Palace is closed on certain religious holidays — confirm availability with your concierge. Dress modestly for all historical and religious sites.

day_by_day.morning: A full day dedicated to the beach and ocean. Begin with an early morning private yacht charter departing from the resort's jetty. Cruise along Cambodia's pristine coastline toward the outer islands — Koh Tang or Koh Prins — uninhabited paradises with crystal-clear turquoise waters and vibrant coral reefs. Enjoy private snorkeling and swimming in secluded bays.
day_by_day.afternoon: Anchor near a deserted island for a private beach picnic prepared by the yacht's onboard chef — fresh ceviche, grilled lobster, tropical fruits, and chilled Champagne. Spend the afternoon swimming, paddleboarding, kayaking, or simply relaxing in the sun on a pristine white sand beach with no other tourists in sight.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort as the sun sets over the Gulf of Thailand. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed evening — perhaps a private bonfire on the beach with cocktails, followed by a light dinner at the resort's beachfront grill.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before boarding the yacht.
meals.lunch: Private gourmet beach picnic on a deserted island — prepared by the yacht's onboard chef with fresh seafood, tropical fruits, and Champagne.
meals.dinner: Casual beachfront grill dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — grilled whole fish, prawns, and local vegetables with craft cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: Private yacht charters should be booked at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and reef-safe snorkeling gear. November sea conditions are generally calm and ideal for island hopping.

day_by_day.morning: Cultural immersion day. Arrange a private cooking class with a renowned local Cambodian chef — visit a traditional morning market to handpick fresh ingredients including lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and local spices. Learn the art of preparing classic Khmer dishes such as Fish Amok (Cambodia's national dish), Lok Lak, and Mango Sticky Rice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Buddhist pagoda (wat) near the resort for a cultural and spiritual experience. Meet with a resident monk for a private blessing ceremony and an insightful conversation about Theravada Buddhism's role in Cambodian daily life. Afterward, explore local artisan workshops — observe traditional Cambodian silk weaving, silver crafting, and lacquerware painting, with the opportunity to purchase premium handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your morning cooking class — a private dinner set in the resort's garden or on the beach, featuring the dishes you prepared, paired with carefully selected Cambodian craft beers or wines. Finish the evening with a traditional Khmer dessert tasting.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the cooking class venue or a local premium eatery near the market.
meals.dinner: Private dinner featuring dishes personally prepared during the morning cooking class, served in a special setting arranged by the resort.

day_by_day.notes: Modest dress is required when visiting Buddhist temples — bring a sarong or light scarf to cover shoulders and knees. Photography inside the pagoda may require permission — ask your guide. Purchase locally made silk scarves or silver jewelry as premium souvenirs to support local artisans.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kep — a charming former French colonial seaside resort town approximately 25 km from Kampot, known for its famous crab market and pepper plantations. Depart by private luxury vehicle. Begin with a visit to Kep National Park — a lush forested hill offering jungle hiking trails with panoramic views of the Gulf of Thailand and nearby Vietnamese islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the famous Kep Crab Market — a lively waterfront market where local fishermen sell freshly caught blue swimming crabs. Arrange a private tasting experience at a premium crab shack — enjoy Kep's signature dish: fresh crab stir-fried with Kampot pepper, one of the world's most prized and aromatic peppers. Afterward, take a short detour to a Kampot pepper farm for a private guided tour, learning about the cultivation and global export of this legendary spice.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Wind down with a sunset yoga session or a soothing spa treatment. Enjoy a refined dinner at the resort, incorporating Kampot pepper into the evening's menu as a nod to the day's discovery.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure.
meals.lunch: Premium crab lunch at Kep's waterfront — fresh blue crab with Kampot pepper, grilled squid, and local vegetables with chilled white wine.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — chef's special menu featuring Kampot pepper-infused dishes with fresh local seafood.

day_by_day.notes: Kep and Kampot are excellent day-trip destinations from the southern coast resort area. The pepper farm visits are best arranged in advance through the concierge. Kampot pepper is a UNESCO-recognized product — consider purchasing premium-grade pepper as a high-quality gift or souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — dedicated to ultimate luxury and relaxation. Begin with a private sunrise meditation session on the beach led by a resort wellness guide, followed by a bespoke spa morning — choose from a full-body Khmer herbal wrap, hot stone massage, or a rejuvenating facial using locally sourced ingredients such as turmeric, coconut oil, and jasmine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a leisurely afternoon at the resort's private beach — enjoy watersports of your choice (jet skiing, stand-up paddleboarding, or windsurfing), read by the infinity pool, or take a final snorkeling excursion in the resort's house reef. Visit the resort's boutique to select premium Cambodian handicrafts, silks, and artisanal goods as final souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner — the resort arranges a special private dining experience on a candlelit floating platform or overwater deck (if available), featuring a bespoke seven-course Cambodian fine-dining menu curated by the executive chef. Toast the journey with a vintage Champagne selected by the resort's sommelier, and enjoy live traditional Cambodian music performed softly in the background.

meals.breakfast: Lavish breakfast at the resort — full à la carte with fresh tropical juices, Eggs Benedict, Cambodian rice porridge, and pastries.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled tiger prawns, green papaya salad, and fresh coconut water.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell seven-course private fine-dining experience — bespoke Cambodian tasting menu with Champagne and wine pairings, live traditional music, and a personalized dessert presentation.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the farewell dinner experience at least 2–3 days in advance through the resort concierge to allow for special arrangements. Request a personalized menu card as a keepsake. Confirm departure logistics with the concierge — luggage packing, checkout time, and airport transfer for the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — leisurely checkout day. Enjoy a final breakfast at the resort with ocean views, savoring the last moments of the Cambodian coastline. Take a slow walk along the beach for a final sunrise stroll. Exchange contact details with resort staff, collect any stored luggage, and finalize gratuities for guides and resort team members.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to the nearest international airport (Phnom Penh or Sihanoukville) for departure. Arrive at the airport with ample time for premium check-in, lounge access, and duty-free shopping. Pick up final Cambodian souvenirs — Kampot pepper, Cambodian silk, silver jewelry, or artisan coffee from the Cardamom Mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry with you the memories of ancient temples, pristine beaches, rich Khmer culture, and the extraordinary warmth of Cambodian hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — full à la carte with fresh tropical fruits, Cambodian rice dishes, eggs to order, and premium coffee.
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport business lounge or a premium airport restaurant before departure.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at destination upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm airport transfer timing the night before with the concierge. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Cambodia's currency is the Riel (KHR), but USD is widely accepted — ensure any remaining local currency is exchanged before departure. A Cambodia departure tax may be included in your ticket — confirm with your airline.
